questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My major at KU. As a student majoring in Korean studies any other destination whould not have made sense.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall it was really great, some few things at the foreign university could have been better but overall great!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: My classmates from Denmark, who arrived earlier than me helped me get to my place of stay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: we had an online orientation, which was fine, but my assigned buddy was not helpfull at all as she did not help me at all or keep in contact.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Only one option, university Campus international dormitory

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: the dormitory had a shared microwave, and hot water tank, so one could make cub noodles. But no cooking appliences were allowed in the rooms. you could buy a meal plan for the campus cafeterias, but i didn't buy it. Campus cafeterias were delicious and there were a lot of cheap options for eating out as per culture at the back of the campus close to the dormitory.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The dormitory is very dirty when you move in and the first thing you should do is clean it. You have to bring your own bed sheets and linens. the dormitory is located on a big hill so its a bit tiring going back and forth. the rules might sound strict, but the school don't check or care about them,

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: lots of space for clothes and stuff, an okay big bathroom (bigger than my copemhagen bathroom). the rooms are for 2 people and they will put you in a room with someone from your home university if available

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: there was a bit confusing with the dates for class registration but else good.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: you choose subjects 2 weeks time before semster start, try the clases for a week and then you have a chance to change.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: the international office at the university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: i got everything i wanted. i changed one class, as it was not for foreigners.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: while registrating for classes remember to look for after school clubs and join those. take clases in korean as Kangwon does not offer sprogskole as part of the deal with KU.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Pretty easy and straightforward

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: the classes were kinda easy and didn't give much homework.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: not very dissimilar, very dissursive

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: korean poems and songs (kor), 위국인을 위한 생활 한국어, korean language and culture through media and film, korean broadcasting culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: korean poems and songs

Additional comments:

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: school festival and sports clubs, hanbok dressing etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: school festival

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go to gapyeong and nami island on the way to seoul

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: quite easy as my major is korean studies and i knew what to expect. been there before

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: be extroverted

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the part were people would stare at me beacuse i'm so white

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the helpsomeness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: make korean friends, do not relay on your danish friends, have fun

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: come before classes start and stay as long as possible

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: my korean friends

questions.answer: Living without a real korean phone number

questions.answer: no
